text:
alex: Hey team — customer on prod is seeing repeated SSE disconnects and a stream that cuts off mid-response. They say it happens when their mobile app is backgrounded and comes back. Repro steps below.

mira: can you paste the server logs? 

alex: sure, excerpt from our streaming runtime at time of disconnect: 
```
2026-02-12T14:22:03.123Z INFO stream: client_id=acct-42 conn=10.1.8.9:43210 write_len=8192 err=EAGAIN
2026-02-12T14:22:03.456Z WARN stream: backpressure: sock_send_queue=983040 client_buf=1.2MB threshold=1MB action=abort
2026-02-12T14:22:03.457Z ERROR stream: aborting stream: reason=slow_consumer_breach code=SSE_ABORT_WRITEBACKPRESSURE
```
mira: looks like our backpressure threshold triggered and we aborted. That second line shows sock_send_queue high. Do we have any tcp retransmit counters? 

jamie-oncall: oncall here, flagging eng-runtime. alex, please run `ss -m` and `ss -ti` on the host while reproducing, and collect `netstat -s | grep retransm` and `sudo perf top` if possible. Also attach the request_id for the failed stream.

alex: request_id=f71a2b9c, running ss output now: 
```
Transport Total send buf: 16384
Transport Total receive buf: 87380
ESTAB  local 10.1.8.9:443 peer 10.2.4.21:54012 snd-q: 7680 rcv-q: 0
```
mira: client is clearly slow (snd-q non-zero). Could be mobile OS throttling the TCP read loop. Any client logs?

alex: customer sent client logs: their mobile SDK shows 'socket temporarily unavailable' and retries every 2s. They also do a full reconnect on any partial chunk.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1285 (streaming slow-consumer abort loop). Assigned to eng-runtime. :rotating_light: 

mira: plausible repro: background the app, pause reads for ~5s, then resume. Our runtime currently aborts if client_buf > 1MB for >200ms. That prevents resource buildup but causes partial output for them.

jamie-oncall: short-term mitigation suggestions: 1) lower our abort aggressiveness for mobile clients by increasing threshold to 2MB or duration to 1s for the customer’s tenant; 2) enable chunked keepalive pings so client has to acknowledge small frames; 3) recommend client change to not reopen connection immediately but resume reading.

alex: can we flip tenant-level override? we can, but worried about DoS if many slow clients.

mira: create a canary: increase threshold for just acct-42 for 24h while we gather traces. Add a rate cap: max simultaneous slow-consumers per node = 3.

jamie-oncall: steps to collect repro traces: 1) enable socket-level histograms (snd-q distribution) 2) enable debug-level stream traces for request_id f71a2b9c 3) collect tcpdump -n host 10.2.4.21 and capture 30s around disconnect (rotate 1MB) 4) ask customer to run a simple python SSE consumer reproducer I can share.

alex: sending reproducer: 
```
# python minimal slow-reader
import sseclient, requests, time
r = requests.get('https://api.redwood.com/v1/eventstream', stream=True, headers={'Authorization':'Bearer TOK'})
client = sseclient.SSEClient(r)
for i,event in enumerate(client.events()):
    print(event.data[:200])
    if i==3:
        time.sleep(6)  # simulate backgrounded app
```
mira: nice. also try node: set highWaterMark small and pause the stream to simulate backpressure.

billing-bot: FYI customer reported a billing spike due to repeated reconnects — ticket BILL-789. May need to offer credits if we find server behavior caused rapid reconnect loop.

jamie-oncall: agreed. collect metrics: reconnect-rate, bytes-per-session, token-usage for acct-42. If server aborted mid-chunk, that can cause duplicate token charges on reconnect.

alex: putting canary in place now (acct override). Will post runbook: toggle backpressure.threshold and backpressure.window_ms for tenant.

mira: long-term fixes: 1) smarter slow-consumer classification: mark mobile UA and apply softer heuristics 2) implement graceful pause/backpressure feedback via a control event so clients can ack slower reads 3) expose SDK helpers to auto-buffer and resume without reconnect.

jamie-oncall: thanks. eng-runtime, please pick this up in priority. If we confirm server abort is the root cause, coordinate with billing for crediting.

alex: any other checks? I also asked customer for platform version, NAT gateway logs, and mobile SDK version.

mira: Good. Keep thread updated. If you need a hand with packet analysis ping #eng-runtime and drop the pcap. :thumbsup:
